lineas.texto: In 2023, an Iraqi refugee named Salwan Momika burned copies of the Quran in public squares in Stockholm. Sweden let him. That is what Sweden was — a country where you could do the most offensive thing imaginable, and the state would stand between you and the consequences.

On the twenty-ninth of January, 2025, Momika was live-streaming from his apartment in Södertälje when men came through the door and shot him dead. On camera. Swedish court documents later named a suspect: a twenty-four-year-old Syrian man, living in Sweden.
And Sweden had already paid for those burnings once. Turkey spent months blocking Swedish entry into NATO over them, demanding extraditions. A country's entire defence policy, held up over a book.
This is not a story about one dead man. It is the day Sweden stopped being able to guarantee the one thing it was famous for.
You can still say anything in Sweden. You just might not survive saying it.
Should he have been allowed to burn it? Yes or no — comments.
